transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-28
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam (Solstice Head of ML), Priya (CTO), Jordan (SRE), Asha (Product)

Summary: (auto) quick discovery to understand Solstice's migration from OpenAI -> dedicated/private, confirm compatibility with existing vLLM/TGI stacks, evaluate eval parity and latency/cost tradeoffs, security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SSO), next steps to run benchmarks and share pricing.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm an AE at Redwood, with Ethan my SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Liam: Doing well, thanks. excited to dig in, we've been evaluating options to move off OpenAI for production due to cost and data controls.
[00:14] Priya: hi all, want to make sure we cover security and network constraints, we run PHI in a few flows, so compliance is key.
[00:22] Ethan: great, we'll cover dedicated and private options; also want to understand your current runtime stack — are you using vLLM or TGI in-house?
[00:30] Liam: we actually have a hybrid — inference for some endpoints is via OpenAI's API, for on-prem experiments we use vLLM on a few nodes and some TGI forks. so compatibility and model parity is the big question.
[00:43] Maya: ok makes sense. first question — what's your target latency SLO and token volumes?
[00:48] Liam: low-latency for chat is about 200-400ms p50 for short prompts, p95 can be higher, but we want under 1s p95. token volume right now is ~15M tokens/month but doubling in next 6 months.
[01:05] Ethan: thanks. rough mental model — Hosted Redwood is the fastest path, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation which helps with cost at scale and regulatory needs. Private/VPC is for when you need customer-managed networking and KMS. is data residency also a requirement?
[01:20] Priya: maybe, we have some customers in EU that require EU-only processing for certain features. also SOC2 type II is required.
[01:28] Maya: we have SOC2 and can provide audit logs; for EU residency we can route to region, and Dedicated or Private can be provisioned in region.
[01:35] Jordan: on networking — we need to avoid opening wide egress; can we do VPC peering and private endpoints? any latency penalty?
[01:42] Ethan: yes VPC peering / private endpoints supported for Dedicated + Private. latency depends on region and peering; usually negligible, but we do recommend colocating in same cloud region and testing.
[01:52] Asha: technical Q — we've built a lot of tooling around vLLM caching and KV cache management. how similar is Redwood's runtime? will we need to rework?
[02:01] Ethan: good question. our serving runtime supports KV/ prefix caching and continuous batching. we expose controls for cache durations and batching windows. in many cases you can keep your same caching logic; we can also integrate at the request layer so minimal code changes.
[02:13] Liam: compatibility — will our prompts behave the same? we've trained against Anthropic and OpenAI — eval parity is a concern.
[02:21] Ethan: parity depends on model family; if you pick the same base open model (e.g., Llama2/Redwood-verified builds) you should see similar outputs, but there are small differences. we recommend running an eval bench with your prompts — we'll run that for you and compare against OpenAI/Anthropic baseline.
[02:34] Priya: can you run a diff for hallucination and alignment metrics? we have safety thresholds.
[02:38] Ethan: yes we can include safety checks in the eval suite — hallucination rate, factuality, and token-level latency.
[02:44] Liam: what about model variants — can Redwood fallback to smaller quantized models when load spikes?
[02:50] Maya: yes, routing policies can fallback to cheaper quantized variants, or a different region. that keeps the system online and is configurable by policy.
[02:58] Jordan: curious about kernel/runtime choices — you mentioned quantization-friendly execution paths and kernel selection earlier in the deck. how automated is that?
[03:05] Ethan: the runtime profiles models and selects optimized kernels depending on arch, sequence length distribution, and hardware (A100 vs H100 vs CPU quantized). we also have recommendations for quantization that we test in our optimize toolkit.
[03:18] Liam: cost — how big is the delta vs OpenAI for our profile? openai heavy chat for us is expensive.
[03:23] Maya: rough numbers depend on tokens and batching. Dedicated usually reduces per-token cost by 30-60% at scale compared to hosted public APIs, but there's capacity commitment. we'll share a sizing + pricing calc.
[03:34] Priya: security — KMS/HSM: we want customer-managed keys and key rotation. supported?
[03:39] Ethan: yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS integration (cloud KMS or external HSM) and audit logs; Private allows you to keep keys fully customer-managed.
[03:47] Asha: do you offer SAML/SSO and RBAC for multi-tenant teams?
[03:51] Maya: yes SAML, SCIM and RBAC are standard for enterprise plans.
[03:55] Liam: network egress — for on-prem some of our data must not leave our VPC. can private deployment be air-gapped?
[04:02] Ethan: we offer on-prem packages for air-gapped environments; depending on the feature set there may be tradeoffs for observability retention, but core inference and audit logs work.
[04:12] Priya: ok good. can we talk about the migration path — we don't want downtime.
[04:18] Maya: typical migration is phased: start with non-critical endpoints on Dedicated in parallel, run canary traffic, compare outputs via eval harness, then cutover. we support traffic split/rollouts and automatic fallback to Hosted if needed.
[04:31] Liam: on benchmarking — what does the eval harness need from us?
[04:34] Ethan: a representative prompt set (100–1k prompts), classification of expected outputs, and performance targets. we'll run parity tests against your OpenAI baseline and share metrics (latency, cost, accuracy, hallucination).
[04:47] Liam: do you support streaming responses and function/tool calling? a lot of our product relies on streaming partial tokens for UX.
[04:53] Ethan: yes streaming and function calling supported; the runtime optimizes for streaming latency specially when batching is enabled.
[05:00] Asha: any gotchas with TGI/vLLM? sometimes those runtimes have different tokenization defaults and subtle output differences.
[05:06] Ethan: tokenization differences are a common source of parity drift. we recommend normalizing tokenization and including it in the eval. we can run the same tokenizer as part of the harness.
[05:16] Priya: SLA and uptime — what uptime do you guarantee for Dedicated?
[05:20] Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; exact terms are in the contract but we can discuss.
[05:26] Jordan: operations — how do we integrate observability? we have Datadog and internal tracing.
[05:31] Ethan: console exposes per-route latency, token-level cost breakdowns, traces and we have Datadog integrations and tracing hooks. logs can be streamed to your SIEM.
[05:42] Liam: legal/procurement timeline — we prefer a month to proof-of-concept then expand. what's typical lead time?
[05:48] Maya: for Dedicated provisioning it's usually 2–4 weeks for initial capacity; Private/on-prem longer. contracts depend on enterprise terms but we can accelerate for pilots.
[05:58] Priya: can you support regional data residency in EU for dedicated nodes?
[06:03] Maya: yes, we can allocate Dedicated capacity in EU regions, and control where inference runs.
[06:09] Liam: curious about model onboarding — we trained a custom fine-tuned model with some RLHF and want to deploy it. how do we get it onto Redwood Dedicated?
[06:17] Ethan: you can upload model artifacts to your private registry or we can ingest them; for Private you can keep everything in your VPC. we validate artifact formats (Transformers, GGUF, etc.) and run a quick compatibility test.
[06:29] Asha: format — do you support GGUF and standard HF checkpoints?
[06:33] Ethan: yes, GGUF supported; we also accept standard Hugging Face formats and can help convert.
[06:38] Liam: any performance differences for custom fine-tunes vs base models?
[06:41] Ethan: depends on architecture and quantization; our kernel selection still applies and we test performance during onboarding. sometimes fine-tunes have slightly different memory profiles.
[06:52] Maya: let's talk about next steps — we'll run a parity benchmark, share pricing, and schedule a network deep dive. are there any blockers?
[06:58] Priya: just making sure legal can get SOC2 and data processing addendum.
[07:03] Maya: got it, we'll attach SOC2 and DPA.
[07:07] Liam: one more — can we do a small perf test with our prompts now? like an initial smoke run?
[07:12] Ethan: yes we can run a small smoke test — it'd be limited but good to catch tokenization and integration issues. we'll need your prompt set and API keys/ingest method.
[07:21] Jordan: on logging retention — we want 90 days for diagnostics, is that configurable?
[07:26] Ethan: yes observability retention tiers are configurable; longer retention is a paid add-on.
[07:32] Asha: and about cost controls — can we set route-based budgets and quotas for teams?
[07:36] Maya: yes quota per API key/route and alerting for spend thresholds.
[07:41] Liam: any references for customers who've migrated from OpenAI to Dedicated? would be helpful to see a case study.
[07:46] Maya: we'll share a couple of anonymized case studies and a migration checklist.
[07:50] Priya: perfect.

[07:55] Recap and close:
Maya: action items — we'll send pricing + sizing, SOC2 + security docs, schedule technical deep dive. Ethan will run eval/harness with prompts once Liam shares them. Jordan to share network diagram.
Liam: sounds good, thanks.
Priya: thanks all.

[08:10] End of call.
